overview: April 1935 memo: a Chinese seaman killed another aboard the Rashin Maru near Hawaii; Japan's Embassy sought custody pending deportation to Japan, but Justice found no federal violation and left Hawaiian territorial jurisdiction to local authorities, letting the master retake custody.

people.name: Eugene H. Dooman
people.role: Department of State official in the Division of Far Eastern Affairs; participant and apparent author of the memorandum

people.name: Mr. Ramsay
people.role: Official of the Criminal Division, Department of Justice

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation on the RASHIN MARU homicide
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Records diplomatic and interdepartmental discussions over custody and jurisdiction following the killing of a Chinese seaman aboard the Japanese steamship RASHIN MARU near Hawaii.
subfiles.summary: Kawahara reports a Chinese seaman killed another aboard the Rashin Maru near Hawaii, seeking custody for deportation to Japan; Justice found no federal violation, deferred to Hawaiian territorial law, and allowed the master to resume custody, which Kawahara appreciated.

interest: Shows unclear 1935 criminal jurisdiction over a Chinese crewman's killing aboard a Japanese ship near Hawaii.
